name: Polling in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village in the Inntal with views of the Telfser Berge and its own Baggersee as a local recreation area.
text:
Overview

Polling in Tirol is situated in the sun-drenched central Upper Inn Valley in the district of Innsbruck-Land at an altitude of 615 metres, located on the southern riverbank roughly 20 kilometres west of Innsbruck between Telfs and Inzing. This peaceful residential community is home to approximately 1,370 inhabitants and covers 5.7 square kilometres. The municipal area comprises the historic core of Polling-Dorf on the fertile valley floor along with the scenic scattered hamlet of Pollingberg, perched on a sunny low-mountain terrace between 780 and 860 metres above sea level. Geographically, Polling provides sweeping panoramic vistas of the colossal southern face of Mount Hohe Munde and the rugged Mieming Chain. The village has lovingly preserved its rural charm, featuring traditional timber farmhouses, colourful cottage gardens, and vibrant community traditions, offering quiet relaxation combined with fast access to Innsbruck.

History

Polling is one of the oldest historically documented settlements in the entire central Inn Valley. Founded by Bavarian settlers, the village was first recorded in 763 under the name Pollinga in the registers of the monastery of Scharnitz/Freising; its name likely traces back to the clan of an early chieftain named Pollo. For centuries, rural life centred on crop farming, livestock, and forestry. A poignant chapter occurred during the catastrophic plague epidemic of 1636: fulfilling a solemn vow, surviving villagers established a plague cemetery and chapel. On this sacred ground, the present Baroque Parish Church of St. Roch was constructed in 1744 and consecrated in 1761; dedicated to Saint Roch, protector against pestilence, the church features splendid ceiling frescoes painted in 1756 by Anton Kirchebner. In the 18th century, legendary cartographer Peter Anich surveyed the slopes of Pollingberg for his groundbreaking Atlas Tyrolensis map.

Getting There

Reaching Polling in Tirol is fast and convenient by private vehicle or public transport. Motorists take the Inntal Autobahn A12, exiting at Telfs-Ost or Zirl-West and following federal road B171 or the L11 provincial road, arriving from Innsbruck in just 20 minutes. Rail passengers use the nearby Tyrolean S-Bahn stations (lines S4 and S5) at Flaurling (1.5 km west) or Hatting (2 km east), both served at frequent 30-minute intervals from Innsbruck Central Station. In addition, VVT regional bus route 4165 stops directly in the village centre, connecting to Telfs, Zirl, and Innsbruck. Cyclists can pedal along the flat Inn Valley Cycle Path R3 along the southern riverbank.

Tips

A lovely scenic walking area is the sunny terrace of Pollingberg: quiet trails wind past traditional wooden mountain farmsteads offering panoramic views over the valley. The popular Peter-Anich-Weg trail connects Pollingberg through pleasant woodland with neighbouring Hattingberg and Flaurling. Ambitious alpine hikers can ascend towards the summit cross of Pollinger Kreuz (2,196 m) and the alpine pastures of Flaurlinger Alm. Nature enthusiasts will appreciate the close proximity to the Gaisau Nature Reserve just east of the village, one of Tyrol's most valuable riparian wetlands. On hot summer days, the natural Pollinger Baggersee lake on the eastern outskirts offers refreshing family swimming, while the Inn Cycle Route and Tyrolean Way of St. James provide flat touring.
